text: Elephant Memory 是面向 DSH web 客户端的跨会话记忆插件。它以独立 Endless preset 替换普通压缩流程，在每轮开始时用有界摘要视图承载项目中的历史，并可自动补入相关原文片段。主要功能包括后台生成和合并摘要、按问题排序检索历史、逐层展开摘要查看原始消息、按短语或正则搜索记录，以及整理带日期的决定和规则。它还提供浏览器记忆查看界面和 recall、zoom、date 等 agent 工具，适合需要在多个聊天间延续上下文并追溯原话的 DSH 用户。摘要使用当前聊天的模型与提供方；默认记忆目录位于 DSH home 下的 endless。

Elephant Memory carries project history across DSH chats. Its Endless preset starts each turn with a bounded summary and retrieves relevant original passages. Features include ranked recall, phrase search, summary expansion, a dated decision journal, and a browser view of stored memories.
我想让不同聊天里的 agent 记得之前讨论过的内容。
能不能在新一轮开始时自动找回相关的旧消息？
想搜索以前的聊天记录，并查看命中的原话和日期。
让 DSH 把很长的对话压成摘要，同时还能逐层展开旧内容。
Can my agent bring relevant details from earlier chats into a new turn automatically?
I need to search old conversations and inspect the exact messages behind a summary.
Elephant Memory 的功能「跨聊天摘要」：每轮开始时将项目历史以有界摘要视图放入上下文，后台逐步写入并合并摘要，避免把完整历史都放进当前请求。
Elephant Memory 的功能「历史召回」：agent 可用 recall 工具按问题检索历史消息，返回按相关性排序的原文片段及日期，供回答时参考。
Elephant Memory 的功能「查看摘要原文」：agent 调用 zoom 并给出摘要行编号和范围，可逐层打开摘要，最终读取对应的完整历史消息。
Elephant Memory 的功能「按原文搜索」：agent 使用 recall_search 输入短语或正则表达式，在历史消息中查找匹配项并获得日期、类型和片段。
Elephant Memory 的功能「决策日志」：插件在后台从已结束的对话轮次中提取带日期的决定和规则，并将日志附在记忆视图之后。
Elephant Memory 使用前须知：摘要和召回扩展由当前聊天所用模型处理，会消耗该提供方的用量；记忆默认写入 DSH home 下的 endless 目录。（见 lib/engine.js:47）

dsh-elephant-memory README · Introduction：

dsh-elephant-memory README · Elephant Memory：**Your DeepSeek agent can look back across its chats.**

[](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-elephant-memory)
[](https://github.com/Shtukbase/elephant-memory/actions/workflows/test.yml)

dsh-elephant-memory README · Elephant Memory：Elephant Memory is a plugin for the [DeepSeek harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness)
(`dsh`). Every chat you have in a folder becomes one long memory: each new turn
starts with a bounded summary of earlier turns, matching source passages and a
dated decision journal. The agent can open any summary line down to the exact
words. Keeping history does not guarantee that a model finds or uses every fact.

dsh-elephant-memory README · Ranked recall and the decision journal：The Endless preset retains the ordinary coding tools and all earlier look-back
tools. It adds `recall(question)`, a ranked search over spoken messages, with
short query expansion on the conversation's own model and account. Expansion
has a six-second deadline; failure leaves the original query usable. It never
searches another project's memory.
section: Ranked recall and the decision journal

text:
dsh-elephant-memory README · Ranked recall and the decision journal：Before a turn's first model request, automatic recall can add up to twenty
passages, within a 40,000-byte content budget plus framing. Passages follow the
summary view, not the standing context. Irrelevant messages add no block. Manual
recall freezes its sources before expansion and forwards cancellation to the
model request. Raw `recall_search` and `zoom` remain available for tool traces,
which ranked recall deliberately excludes.
section: Ranked recall and the decision journal

text:
dsh-elephant-memory README · Ranked recall and the decision journal：The preset also extracts decisions, rules, reversals and open work from finished
spoken turns in the background. Four turns, or 16,000 characters of split long
messages, form one extraction window. Each saved batch binds its exact source
and predecessor; a changed source invalidates its dependent cache. A failed
write advances nothing. A restart resumes saved progress. There is no bundled
conversation or static research journal.
section: Ranked recall and the decision journal

text:
dsh-elephant-memory README · Ranked recall and the decision journal：The request's journal is limited to 16,000 bytes. Its cache can grow with the
history. It is derived history, not new instructions or current repository
state; it may lag behind incoming turns. Summaries must be ready before a turn
starts, but a journal still being written does not hold that turn. Recall-only
answers use memory; a request to change files still requires the normal work.
The journal is model-written: valid source references do not guarantee its
paraphrases or speaker attribution. Look back at exact words when accuracy
matters; a source hash alone does not establish semantic support.
section: Ranked recall and the decision journal

text:
dsh-elephant-memory README · Ranked recall and the decision journal：For custom hosts, `ledger` is off until explicitly enabled. The preset enables
`ledger`, `lookBackRules`, `recall`, `autoRecall` and `lineTools`. A host can turn
off automatic passages with `autoRecall: false`, or journal extraction with
`ledger: false`. `recallMost` accepts 1–50; `ledgerBytes` accepts 512–64,000.
No three-step cap or tool-free answer mode is imposed on coding sessions.
section: Ranked recall and the decision journal

(first published as OptChat). Source, issues and releases:

dsh-elephant-memory README · Install：The source release is **0.4.0**. Install that exact version from its tag; the
npm registry version can lag behind the source release:

```sh
git clone --branch v0.4.0 --depth 1 https://github.com/Shtukbase/elephant-memory.git elephant-memory
dsh plugin --profile web add ./elephant-memory
```

The registry command, `dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-elephant-memory`, installs
the version currently published there, not necessarily this source release.

dsh-elephant-memory README · Install：The plugin supports Node 22 or newer; the acceptance runs used Node 25.2.1.
Use that runtime for the current harness CLI: Node 23.10.0 can exit without
starting it because it lacks `import.meta.main`. You need `pnpm` on your `PATH` (the harness's plugin command
runs it), and harness **0.2.1-alpha.1 or newer, below 0.3**
(`npm install -g @deepseek-ai/dsh@0.2.1-alpha.1` installs the tested version).

dsh-elephant-memory README · Install：1. **Add the plugin to a profile.** The web profile is the one `dsh web` starts;
   the command creates it if it does not exist yet:

Use the source-folder command above for this release, or the registry
   command for its separately published version.

dsh-elephant-memory README · Install：`add` also takes a folder that holds this package or a `.tgz` made by
   `npm pack`. Because the package ships a bundle patch, `add` also turns that
   patch on. The harness checks the package's `peerDependencies` at install and
   at every start, and refuses a harness outside 0.2.x.

2. **Start, or restart, the harness:** `dsh web`. It prints the address of its
   page; open it in a browser.

dsh-elephant-memory README · Version 0.4.0：The default view is twice the size: `viewBytes` 128,000 becomes 256,000 and
`viewFloorBytes` 64,000 becomes 128,000. A long chat then spends longer before
its oldest lines are merged, more of it is read word for word, and the summary
of the same history is read back more often. The measurement behind the change
was a live memory of 544 messages, of which the view showed 173 lines; a memory
already on disk rebuilds to the new ceiling once its view sits under the new
floor.

dsh-elephant-memory README · Version 0.3.0：Ranked recall and automatic source passages complement the existing summary,
raw search and zoom tools. Query expansion is bounded and keeps the original
query on failure. The Endless preset enables a bounded decision journal with
durable progress, restart recovery and source-change invalidation. Ordinary
coding tools remain available; the plugin does not set an effort or call cap.
Manual recall has readable transcript rows with opening, closing and reload
coverage. The supported harness floor is 0.2.1-alpha.1.

dsh-elephant-memory README · Choose the Endless preset：A preset is what the harness calls a mode. The plugin adds one, **endless**,
shown as *Endless* in the mode list of a new conversation. It is the harness's
Creator mode with this memory in place of the usual compaction (compaction is
how the harness shortens a long history; this memory replaces it).

dsh-elephant-memory README · Choose the Endless preset：1. Start a new session. Above the message box, next to the workspace, open the
   mode picker (it shows *Standard mode*) and pick **Endless** before the first
   message. A session's mode cannot change after its first message, and every
   new session starts in the default mode again.
2. Work as usual. When a turn ends, it is kept word for word and summarized in
   the background. Every later turn starts from the summary.

dsh-elephant-memory README · Choose the Endless preset：To make Endless the default for new sessions, edit
`$DSH_HOME/profiles/web/cordis.patch.yml` (`$DSH_HOME` is the harness's home
folder, `~/.dsh` unless you set it). The file starts as an empty list, `[]`;
replace that with this list, or add the item to the list already there:

```yaml
- id: agent-preset-registry
  config:
    default: endless
```

dsh-elephant-memory README · Set up a model：The memory uses the chat's own model: whichever model and provider the session
runs also write its summaries. When you switch provider or model in the
composer, the summaries follow at the next turn: the writer uses the route that
turn's own request uses, not the one the chat was created on. The preset's
model context window must be at least **122,560 tokens**. Summary-only hosts
need 65,536; default automatic recall without the journal needs 106,560.
These conservative floors reserve the configured additions. Smaller models
run as ordinary chats without reading or writing this memory.

dsh-elephant-memory README · Set up a model：Choose only a reasoning effort the adapter actually declares. The research
adapter's `medium` setting was cheaper than its `high` setting in the recall
grid. The official DeepSeek adapter declares `off`, `low`, `high` and `max`,
not `medium`; this plugin does not invent that level or change the chat's effort.

dsh-elephant-memory README · Set up a model：1. **DeepSeek's official API** works out of the box: give the harness your key
   in its page's "Add an API key" dialog, or set `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` before
   `dsh web`.
2. **An OpenAI-compatible gateway** goes through the harness's `dsh-llm-pi-ai`
   adapter. This example declares OpenCode Go's endpoint (it requires an
   `x-opencode-session` header) and makes it the default model. Add the items
   to the same `cordis.patch.yml` list:

dsh-elephant-memory README · Set up a model：`apiKeyEnv` names a credential, never the key itself: set it in the
   environment, or in `$DSH_HOME/.credentials.yaml` (`version: 1`, then
   `refs:` with `OPENCODE_GO_API_KEY: "<your key>"`, file mode 0600). The empty
   `off:` level lets the summary writer turn thinking off (deviation 13). A
   declared model without it still works: the writer reads the efforts the
   model declares and asks for the lowest one, or for none when the model
   declares no reasoning at all, and logs that once. Such a model may think on
   every summary, which costs output tokens.

dsh-elephant-memory README · How memory is keyed：A memory belongs to **one mode in one workspace folder**. Every Endless chat in
the same workspace reads and writes the same memory, so a new chat there already
knows the earlier ones and can say which chat something was said in. A chat in
another workspace has a memory of its own. The workspace is the folder shown
next to the mode picker; the web page's first one, *Default workspace*, is
`~/Documents/deepseek-harness/default-workspace`.

dsh-elephant-memory README · How memory is keyed：The memory is plain files under `$DSH_HOME/endless/`. To forget a memory, delete
its folder there (see [Where the files are](#where-the-files-are)).

A program that drives the harness (a "host") can bind a chat to its own key,
an agent and a project, before the chat's first turn; see
[For hosts](#for-hosts).

dsh-elephant-memory README · History：Open the right sidebar and pick **History** on its start page, or type
**/history** in the composer. History shows the memory of the current chat's
folder, and a picker offers any other memory.

dsh-elephant-memory README · History：1. **Conversation** is every turn of every chat, grouped by day. The search box
   finds raw words anywhere in the memory and highlights them.
2. **Remembers** is the list of summary lines the agent starts its next turn
   with. Each line opens into the two lines it was made from, down to the exact
   message.

dsh-elephant-memory README · History：A turn you stop with **Esc** is kept too: your message, whatever the agent
already said (a reply cut short is kept as far as it went), its tool uses and
their results so far, then a note that you stopped it. This holds when you stop
the turn while it is still waiting for the memory, before the agent has said
anything: your message is kept once, and it is not sent again by itself. A
turn cut off because the harness stopped running is kept the same way, and
ends with a note that it was interrupted.

dsh-elephant-memory README · Looking back：1. `zoom(id, n)` opens one summary line into the two lines it was made from;
   `zoom(id, 1)` gives one message whole.
2. `date(id)` gives the date and time of a message.
3. `recall_search(query)` searches every message ever written, word for word,
   for a phrase (any case) or a `/regular expression/`. It returns up to 20 hits.
4. `recall(question)` ranks spoken source passages, expands a short query on
   the chosen route and returns dated words, not a newly generated answer.

dsh-elephant-memory README · Looking back：In the transcript each call shows as one row, *Looked back · «what» · date ·
in «chat»*, which opens to the answer. A memory turn is not marked "Context
compacted", because nothing was lost; a real `/compact` in an ordinary chat is
still marked as usual.

dsh-elephant-memory README · Cost and cache：These numbers come from one measured run: 201 scripted turns on 2026-10-08,
model `deepseek-flash` on DeepSeek's official API, harness 0.2.0-rc.2. The costs
are that run's token counts at DeepSeek's list prices for `deepseek-flash`, read
on 2026-10-09 from the
[pricing page](https://api-docs.deepseek.com/quick_start/pricing). Per million
tokens at peak: $0.006 for cached input, $0.30 for other input, $1.20 for
output. Off-peak is half of each: $0.003, $0.15, $0.60. Peak is 01:00-04:00 and
06:00-10:00 UTC, Monday to Friday, except Chinese public holidays. DeepSeek can
change these, so read the page again before you rely on them.

dsh-elephant-memory README · Cost and cache：| Measure | Result |
|---|---|
| Share of each turn's input read from the provider's cache | median **98.4%** (196 ordinary turns, lowest 95.3%) |
| The one turn right after each merge batch (two in the run) | about **35%** read from cache |
| Wait before a turn starts (summaries still being written) | median 5.1 s, 90% under 7.5 s |
| Cost of the agent's turns | $0.46 at peak, $0.23 off-peak |
| Cost of writing summaries (3,133 calls) | $1.50 at peak, $0.75 off-peak |
| Cost of one turn with its summaries | 0.98 cents at peak, 0.49 cents off-peak |
| Exact-quote recall questions | 7 of 7 answered word for word |

dsh-elephant-memory README · Cost and cache：The summary writer was 76% of the bill. Since that run the writer takes at most
three tries per line instead of five and accepts a line up to 1.25 times the
limit (deviation 12 below), and a retry asks for 0.75 of the limit (deviation 16
below), which should cut its calls. A newer run measured them: 235 scripted
turns on 2026-10-08 with this package as published (0.1.1) in a clean harness
0.2.0-rc.2, the default 128,000-byte ceiling and 64,000-byte floor, and
`deepseek-flash` through OpenCode Go. OpenCode Go is a subscription, so its
costs are the run's token counts at the same DeepSeek list prices. The writer
made 2,119 calls, 9.0 a turn against 15.6 before, and cost $1.23 at peak
($0.61 off-peak); the agent's turns cost $0.51 ($0.26). One turn with its
summaries cost 0.74 cents at peak and 0.37 cents off-peak, and the writer was
71% of that.

dsh-elephant-memory README · Cost and cache：Each summary call also re-reads about 16k cached tokens: the turn's system
prompt and tools, then the compaction view. Since 0.2.0 one call writes up to
six summary lines that are ready at the same time (`writer.batch`, deviation 20
below). A run measured it on 2026-10-08, 17:51-18:51 UTC. It used the same 235
scripted turns, the same harness, the same 128,000/64,000-byte view and
`deepseek-flash` through OpenCode Go, priced at the same DeepSeek list prices.
The writer made 1,498 calls, 6.4 a turn against 9.0 with 0.1.1, and cost
$0.995 at peak ($0.50 off-peak) against $1.23. The agent's turns cost $0.47
($0.24). One turn with its summaries cost 0.62 cents at peak and 0.31 cents
off-peak, 16% less than with 0.1.1. The writer trimmed 87 lines against 94, and
all 12 recall checkpoints were answered right in both runs.

dsh-elephant-memory README · Cost and cache：A short live check on the same day used this package as published, installed
from its `.tgz` into a clean harness 0.2.0-rc.2, with `deepseek-flash` through
OpenCode Go: four Endless chats, six turns. A rule given in the first chat was
recalled, with the chat's name, in the second chat's first turn. After the very
first turn, every turn start read 96.9% to 98.3% of its input from the cache,
except one turn right after the plugin's system prompt was changed. The summary
writer made 22 calls, read 94.4% of their input from the cache, wrote about 145
tokens per call, and trimmed 3 lines.

dsh-elephant-memory README · Configuration：To change a setting, copy the `preset-endless` row from
[`presets/endless.patch.yml`](presets/endless.patch.yml) into your profile's
`cordis.patch.yml` without its `- insert:` line, and edit the `endless-memory`
row. A patch replaces a row's whole `config`, so keep every key.

dsh-elephant-memory README · Configuration：| Key | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `agentName` | `Assistant` | The name the summary lines give the agent's replies in a chat nobody bound. A bound chat uses the display name its host gave, or a name read from the agent's address (`team/agents/release-captain` gives "Release Captain"). No colon, no line break. |
| `you` | `you` | The word the summary lines use for the person. |
| `viewBytes` | `256000` | The summary's ceiling in bytes: once it passes this, one batch of merges brings it down to `viewFloorBytes`. |
| `viewFloorBytes` | half of `viewBytes` | The floor the batch merges down to (128,000 by default). |
| `lineBytes` | `512` | The target size of one summary line, in bytes. |
| `granularity` | `turn` | `turn` keeps one trace message per turn; `step` keeps every tool call and result as its own message (deviation 1). |
| `writer.model` | `''` | Another model **of the chat's own provider** for writing summaries; empty means the chat's model. A `writer.provider` key is refused. |
| `writer.batch` | `6` | The most summary lines one call writes when several are ready at once (deviation 20). `1` is one line per call, as before 0.

dsh-elephant-memory README · Limitations：1. **Small models.** Below the configured context floor a turn runs as an
   ordinary chat, and the log says so once. DeepSeek's official models are far
   above it.
2. **It spends tokens.** Summaries are written in the background by the chat's
   own model on the chat's own provider, never another one. Query expansion and
   the journal spend tokens too. Every writer call is
   logged and totalled in the memory's `usage.jsonl`.
3. **Dynamic additions change the cache suffix.** The first turn after a merge
   batch misses from the first merged line. Journal updates and different recall
   passages can change later input too. Historical summary-only cache shares
   above do not guarantee the new preset's share.
4. **A turn can be refused.** If summary lines are still missing after 180 s,
   the turn ends with one sentence in the chat's refusal line: "The memory of
   earlier messages is not ready yet, so this message will be sent with your
   next one." Its messages wait in the chat's queue and go with your next
   message; the chat stays usable. This happens the same way when the writer is
   slow and when it fails at once on every try. Noth

dsh-elephant-memory README · How it works：The design and every constant come from Taelin's specification; this is a short
tour.

dsh-elephant-memory README · How it works：1. **The log.** The harness's own session logs are the history. When a turn
   ends, its messages are appended to the memory's order of turns, whole, and
   numbered.
2. **The tree.** In the background, each message becomes a summary line of about
   512 bytes. Two neighbouring lines are merged into one, then two of those, and
   so on: a binary tree. A message short enough to fit is its own line, word for
   word.
3. **The view.** A list of lines that covers the whole history, recent messages
   one per line and older ones many per line. It grows by one line per message.
   Once it passes 256 KB, one batch merges the most overdue pairs until it is
   back to 128 KB. A pair's "overdue" score is how long ago it ended, measured in
   its own size: `(T - last) / 2^l`. This reproduces the merge order of Taelin's
   rollback list.
4. **Each turn starts fresh.** Before a turn's first step, the conversation so
   far is replaced by a message holding the view and optional journal, followed
   by matching recalled passages and the new message. The view changes only at
   its end between batches. Dynamic additions follow that stable prefix; their

dsh-elephant-memory README · How it works：How it attaches to the harness, with file and line references, is in
[`SEAMS.md`](SEAMS.md). [`TRY.md`](TRY.md) is a recipe for trying it in an
isolated harness home.

**Thank you, Victor.** The log, the tree, the build order, the merge rule, the
prompts and the constants are from Taelin's specification as rewritten on
2026-10-08. This package is one implementation of that idea.

dsh-elephant-memory README · Deviations from the specification：1. **Granularity `turn` (default).** The specification keeps every tool call and
   result as its own message (`step` here, still available). `turn` keeps, per
   turn, each message of the person, one trace message with the turn's tool
   calls and results, and the final reply. Why: far fewer summary calls, and more
   turns at one line each in the same view. Cost: a trace keeps the first and
   last 30,000 characters of a very long turn (each result already clipped to
   30,000), so the middle of a turn with several huge tool outputs is cut. In
   `step` mode a tool call is one message however long it is.
2. **`recall_search`.** A raw search over the whole history. Why: an item a
   summary dropped can still be found. A `/pattern/` search stops after 2 s,
   because a pattern can take exponential time.
3. **The view is its own message.** The specification sends the view and the new
   message as one user message. Here the view is a message placed before the new
   one, because the harness builds every request from its session log. The
   harness's context messages (skill list, sandbox facts, workspace
   instructions)

dsh-elephant-memory README · For hosts：A program on the same computer can read and bind memories through six methods,
served by the harness's web server as `POST /api/endless.<name>` in the
harness's Remote envelope: `{type: 'client-request', rpcId, method, payload:
{args}}` answered by `{type: 'server-response', rpcId, result}`. Only callers on
this computer are answered, and a request with an `Origin` header (which every
browser page sends) is refused. Times are ISO 8601.

dsh-elephant-memory README · For hosts：| Method | Arguments | Answer |
|---|---|---|
| `endless.bind` | `sessionId, agent, project, agentName?` | `{memoryId}` |
| `endless.memories` | `agent?` | `{memories: [{memoryId, agent, project, turns, firstAt, lastAt, writerUsage}]}` |
| `endless.view` | `memoryId` | `{lines: [{id, n, text, from, to}]}`; `text` is null while a line is not written |
| `endless.zoom` | `memoryId, id, n` | `{lines}` (the two halves), or for `n = 1` `{message: {id, kind, text, at, sessionId, sessionTitle}}` |
| `endless.history` | `memoryId, before?, limit? ≤ 200` | `{turns: [{at, sessionId, sessionTitle, entries: [{id, kind, text}]}], next?}`; pages backwards, oldest first inside a page, and a page stops before 2 MB of text |
| `endless.search` | `memoryId, query, limit? ≤ 50` | `{hits: [{id, at, sessionTitle, kind, snippet}]}`, newest first, raw words, any case |

dsh-elephant-memory README · For hosts：`kind` is `user`, `trace`, `reply` or `work`. `writerUsage` is `{calls,
cacheRead, miss, output}`. A refusal is `{ok: false, error: {code, message}}`
with the code `endless/bad-request`, `endless/unknown-memory`, `endless/no-line`
or `endless/already-bound` (the chat's turns are already in another memory).

The harness's own page reads the five read methods (not `bind`) through
`POST /api/endless-ui.<name>`, behind the harness's own Host and Origin check
and its signed browser cookie.

dsh-elephant-memory README · Where the files are：`<root>` is `$DSH_HOME/endless` unless `root` says otherwise. `memoryId` is the
first 16 hex digits of `sha256(agent + "\n" + project)`; for a chat nobody bound,
`agent` is the id of the mode it runs (`endless`) and `project` its workspace
folder.

dsh-elephant-memory README · Where the files are：| What | Where |
|---|---|
| The memory's key | `<root>/memories/<memoryId>/key.json` |
| Finished turns, in order | `<root>/memories/<memoryId>/order-turn-v1.jsonl` |
| Summary lines | `<root>/memories/<memoryId>/tree-turn-v1/YYYY-MM-DD.jsonl` |
| The view and the writer's view | `view-turn-v1.json`, `compaction-view-turn-v1.json` in the same folder |
| Writer spend | `usage.jsonl` in the same folder, one line per call |
| One-writer lock | `lock` in the same folder |
| A bound chat | `<root>/sessions/<session>.json` |

dsh-elephant-memory README · Where the files are：Every line is written with one write and `fsync`. A torn last line is skipped
at load. Nothing is edited or deleted. The view is saved after every change and
loaded at start, never rebuilt while its file is usable, because a rebuilt view
would differ and lose the cache. With `granularity: step` the file names say
`step` instead of `turn`.

packages, which are peers, so install them first:

dsh-elephant-memory README · Contributing：The browser half is built: `client/` holds its sources, and
`node scripts/build-client.js` writes `lib/client.js` (it also runs on
`npm pack`). Commit both. The tests run the real `lib/client.js` against a fake
of the harness's client, and the engine against a fake of the harness's session
and context owners. A real harness is needed to see anything drawn; see
[`TRY.md`](TRY.md). When the harness changes version, walk the recheck list at
the end of [`SEAMS.md`](SEAMS.md).

dsh-elephant-memory README · Unreleased：1. Summary lines keep the date of each decision, and a merge keeps the dates
   of both its lines, or the latest, marked.
2. Before acting on a remembered decision or fact about files, the agent checks
   `git log` and `git status`; the repository wins over memory.

dsh-elephant-memory README · 0.2.0：1. One summary call writes up to six summary lines that are ready at the same
   time (`writer.batch`, default 6). Each line aims at 0.75 of the limit and is
   judged alone. A line that does not fit is asked again in the same
   conversation. Over 235 scripted turns on `deepseek-flash` the writer made
   29% fewer calls and trimmed fewer lines, and a turn with its summaries cost
   16% less, with the same recall. Set `writer.batch: 1` for one line per call.

dsh-elephant-memory README · 0.1.1：1. A turn stopped with Esc is saved to memory: the person's message, what the
   agent already said, its tool uses with their results so far, and a closing
   note, "stopped by the person". Before, a turn stopped while it waited for
   the memory lost the person's message and was not saved at all, and a turn
   stopped later was saved without saying it had been stopped.
2. A turn cut off because the harness stopped running keeps the person's
   message the same way, and ends with the note "interrupted".
